Wind runs in this tool's GPU shader; OBJ exports the still mesh.BOTANICAL FIELD NOTES

    Fruit / cone reference ↗

    Fruit study shows representative developmental stages independently of the seasonal whole-tree specimen. Cones and cups have separate overlapping geometric scales. Scale counts, micro-relief, seed exposure and material properties are illustrative, not calibrated measurements. Cone opening represents drying rather than the calendar season.

    Root studies expose the modeled below-ground system. Structural, lateral, sinker and fine feeder roots are shown. Species profiles are illustrative biases; soil depth and spread are adjustable, not fixed species measurements. Underground roots stay beneath the ground plane in whole-tree view.

    Botanical reference ↗

    Leaf sizes vary coherently with shoot vigour and node position. Actively extending shoots have smaller, more folded apical leaves; mature set shoots retain fully expanded leaves at their tips. Spring pine shoots include shorter developing needles alongside retained needles. The size control sets a mature target. Growth stages and size gradients are illustrative, not measured phenology.

    What this model represents

    Species architecture includes curved scaffold limbs, unequal crown sectors and connected apical continuations. Willow has arching boughs and long pendulous sprays; oak has sinuous spreading limbs; pine retains uneven whorls and a dominant leader; birch has ascending limbs with drooping fine twigs. These architectural shapes and organ placement are procedural approximations. Whole-tree geometry uses lower organ detail for interactive rendering. Sweet thorn and fever tree use alpha-cut compound-leaf surfaces with procedural leaflet silhouettes and matching cutout shadows; their displayed leaflet counts include those silhouettes. Exports include their colour and opacity maps. Shoot and organ studies resolve separate pinnae, rachises and leaflets; every terminal shoot retains its seasonal foliage; leaf and shoot studies resolve individual organs. Veins have geometric relief in organ studies, a finite blade edge, and procedural normal detail. Wax response uses dielectric microfacet shading. Surface grain, roughness, and thickness are illustrative estimates, not measured or scanned anatomy. Bark studies include geometric relief, branching collars, cut end grain and procedural fine grain. Wood studies are representative segments, not scanned sections of the whole-tree specimen. Junctions use overlapping, shaped collars rather than a watertight mesh union. Bark thickness, relief, fiber scale and material roughness are illustrative estimates. Cellular anatomy, stomatal structure, physiology, disease, and complete growth histories are not modeled. This is not a scientifically validated digital specimen.

    Leaf study displays detached anatomy even in winter. Compound-leaf species show a complete leaf in Leaf study and a single leaflet in Surface study. Wild olive, yellowwood and karee retain winter leaves; sweet thorn and fever tree use a dry/cold deciduous winter profile. Seasonal organ stages are representative, not a local flowering calendar.
